title: Backtracking: permutations
summary: Place an unused value, recurse to fill the rest, then undo the choice and try the next value.

narration.text: No permutations found yet.

Define backtrack: it extends the current arrangement one value at a time.
{path} uses every value: it's a complete permutation.
{path} isn't complete yet. Try each unused value in the next position.
Record it: {len(result)} found so far.
Go back to the previous position and try something else there.
Consider {nums[i]}.
Every value has been tried in this position: go back.
{nums[i]} is already in the arrangement: skip it.
{nums[i]} is free.
Move on to the next value.
Mark {nums[i]} as used.
Place it: the arrangement is now {path}.
Back from exploring every arrangement that starts with {path}.
Take {nums[i]} back off: {path}.
{nums[i]} is free again for other positions.
Every permutation has been found.
There are {len(result)} permutations.
